narration.full_text: Welcome back, students! Let's test your understanding further with some more questions on Control and Coordination. Ready for the challenge? Our first question is: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief. Think about how auxins influence cell growth. The answer is: Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards. These auxins cause cell elongation. In tendrils, auxins move away from the contact point with the support, causing more growth on the side away from the support. This unequal growth makes the tendril coil. Next, illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant. Consider where auxins are formed and their role in various plant parts. The answer to this is: Auxin is formed in the apical meristem of the root and shoot. In the shoot, auxin promotes cell enlargement and inhibits lateral buds, while in the root, it promotes cell division. Now, list in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support. Focus on growth dependence, speed, and direction. Here's the comparison: Mimosa leaves show a growth-independent, fast, and non-directional response. A tendril, however, exhibits a growth-dependent, slow, and directional movement. Our final question for this section: (a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants. (b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement? Think about plant hormones and their roles, and how plants respond to stimuli without muscles. For part (a), the three growth hormones are Auxin, which promotes cell elongation and division; Gibberellins, which help in stem growth; and Cytokinins, which promote cell division and delay leaf ageing. For part (b), plants use electrical and chemical means to convey information. For example, Mimosa pudica leaves fold due to turgor changes, which is a growth-independent movement, while directional movements like a seedling breaking through soil are growth-dependent. Great job, everyone! Keep up the excellent work.

visual_beats.description: Title: More Questions: Control and Coordination
Question: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief.

Answer: Auxins produced in shoot tip move downwards. Cause cell elongation. In tendrils, auxins move away from contact point, causing more growth on the side away from support. Unequal growth makes tendril coil.
Question: Illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant.
Answer: Auxin formed in apical meristem of root/shoot. In shoot, promotes cell enlargement, inhibits lateral buds. In root, promotes cell division.
Question: List in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support.

Answer:
| S.No | Mimosa Leaves | Tendril |
|---|---|---|
| (i) | Growth independent | Growth dependent |
| (ii) | Fast process | Slow process |
| (iii) | Non-directional | Directional |
Question: (a) Write names and one function of three growth hormones in plants. (b) In absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?
Answer (a): Auxin: promotes elongation/division. Gibberellins: stem growth. Cytokinins: cell division, delay leaf ageing.
Answer (b): Plants use electrical/chemical means. Mimosa pudica leaves fold (turgor changes, growth-independent). Directional movements (seedling through soil) are growth-dependent.

visual_content.verbatim_content: Q: How do auxins promote the growth of a tendril around a support? Describe in brief.

A: Auxins produced in the shoot tip move downwards. These auxins cause cell elongation. In the tendrils, auxins move away from the point of contact with the supporting object. More growth occurs on the side away from the support. As a result of unequal growth on the two sides, the tendril coils around the support.
Q: Illustrate with the help of a diagram, the effect of auxins in different parts of a plant.
A: Auxin is formed in the apical meristem of the root and shoot. In the shoot, auxin promotes cell enlargement and inhibits the development of lateral buds. In the root, auxin promotes cell division.
Q: List in tabular form three differences in the movement of leaves of a Touch-me-not plant (the plant of Mimosa family) when touched and movement of a tendril towards a support.

A:
| S.No | Mimosa Leaves | Tendril |
|---|---|---|
| (i) | Growth independent response | Growth dependent response |
| (ii) | It is a fast process | It is a slow process |
| (iii) | It is non-directional | It is directional |

Q: (a) Write the names and one function of each of any three growth hormones in plants.
(b) In the absence of muscle cells, how do plant cells show movement?

A (a): Three growth hormones in plants are-
(i) Auxin: It promotes elongation and division of cell and root formation.
(ii) Gibberellins: They help in the growth of the stem.
(iii) Cytokinins: They promote cell division and delay leaf ageing.

A (b): Plants use electrical and chemical means to convey information. The leaves of Mimosa pudica fold up in response to touch (growth-independent). Directional movement of a seedling breaking through soil is growth-dependent.
